one_liner: C99 JSON DOM parser building the whole tree in one caller-supplied buffer; claims lower parse memory than RapidJSON (unpublished).
what_it_does: A small C library (two .c files, about 2,100 lines) that parses JSON into a read-only DOM stored in one contiguous buffer. The buffer is either a fixed one you pass in (QAJ4C_parse, no heap at all) or one grown through a realloc callback you supply (QAJ4C_parse_dynamic), and QAJ4C_calculate_max_buffer_size returns the exact byte count before you parse. The API is plain C functions over opaque QAJ4C_Value pointers: is_*/get_* accessors, index access into arrays and object members, and key lookup. A Builder constructs DOMs, and sprint or callback printers serialize them. It is not a drop-in for RapidJSON or nlohmann/json.
how_it_is_fast: It is built for low memory, not speed. The parse makes two passes. Pass one validates the input and counts nodes, long-string bytes and each container's member count, keeping the counts in the caller's buffer. Pass two writes the DOM into exactly that many bytes, so arrays and objects become plain C arrays with no per-node allocation and no slack. Each value is a 16-byte tagged cell on 64-bit (12 bytes on 32-bit), strings of up to 10 chars (6 on 32-bit) sit inside the cell, and in-situ mode points strings into the input instead of copying them. Objects with more than two members are sorted with qsort, so key lookup is a binary search.
when_to_use: Firmware or other no-heap targets: parse into a static buffer after sizing it exactly with QAJ4C_calculate_max_buffer_size, or bound it by the formula nodes x 16 B plus the bytes of strings longer than 10 chars.
Read-mostly config, command or telemetry messages where you need O(1) array indexing and key lookup rather than a token stream.
Writable input buffers where copying strings is unaffordable: QAJ4C_parse_insitu leaves only the node cells in the DOM buffer.

Emitting small JSON documents without malloc: build with QAJ4C_Builder in a fixed buffer and stream them out through QAJ4C_print_callback (one char at a time) or QAJ4C_print_buffer_callback (chunks), for example to a UART.
Callers that need a parse error code plus the byte position of the failure (QAJ4C_error_get_errno / QAJ4C_error_get_json_pos).
when_not_to_use: Parsing where throughput matters: the input is scanned twice, numbers go through strtoul/strtod, there is no SIMD, and no timing against RapidJSON exists. yyjson and simdjson have published speed wins.
Round-tripping floating point: the printer formats doubles with "%1.10g" (at most 10 significant digits, so output is lossy), and NaN or Inf values print as null.
Documents nested deeper than 32 levels (max_depth = 32 is hard-coded, so deeper input fails with QAJ4C_ERROR_DEPTH_OVERFLOW), or inputs over 4 GiB (internal offsets are uint32_t).
Code that mutates or grows a parsed DOM: the parse result is const, and arrays and objects cannot be resized (calling set_object/set_array again wastes the old buffer space).
MSVC toolchains, or projects that need upstream fixes: the library is abandoned since 2019 and open bug #8 (the Builder's deduplicate mode asserts instead of overwriting) has no response.

integration.form: source-drop (qajson4c.c + qajson4c_internal.c and 3 headers); the bundled CMake also builds a static and a shared lib
integration.dependencies: none beyond the C standard library, whose calls are funneled through qajson_stdwrap.h so you can supply your own under NO_STDLIB
integration.min_toolchain: C99; GCC or Clang only (structs use __attribute__((packed, aligned))); CMake 2.8.12 for the bundled build; MSVC not supported (Windows via MinGW)
integration.platforms: 32- and 64-bit targets where __WORDSIZE or _WIN32/_WIN64 is defined (otherwise #error). CI covered Linux x86-64 gcc (Travis) and Windows MinGW (AppVeyor). A 2019 branch commit mentions ARM test runs.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Parser state lives on the stack and in the caller's buffer, so separate parses into separate buffers look reentrant from the code. The fatal-error handler is a process-wide global set by QAJ4C_register_fatal_error_function.

gotchas: QAJ4C_parse is lenient by default: it accepts trailing commas, a leading '+', leading zeros and trailing garbage after the root value. Comments (/* */ and //) are accepted even in strict mode. Pass QAJ4C_PARSE_OPTS_STRICT to QAJ4C_parse_opt for tighter validation.

By default, parsed objects with more than 2 members are re-sorted (by key length, then bytes). Index iteration and printing then lose the input key order unless you pass QAJ4C_PARSE_OPTS_DONT_SORT_OBJECT_MEMBERS, and lookup with duplicate keys is undefined.

A type-mismatched accessor (for example QAJ4C_get_int on a string) calls the fatal-error hook, which by default calls raise(SIGABRT). The header comment says it prints to stderr. Check with is_* first, or register your own handler.

The pointer returned by QAJ4C_parse_dynamic is the start of the realloc'd buffer, and you must free() it; only the nativejson-benchmark harness shows this, not the README or header. In-situ parsing and the *_by_ref builder calls keep pointers into your strings, so those strings must outlive the DOM.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: jsmn is also allocation-free C, but it only returns tokens; qajson4c gives you a real DOM with array indexing and binary-search key lookup inside one precisely sized buffer. Against yyjson or simdjson, which have measured speed wins over RapidJSON, pick qajson4c only when a computable memory bound with no heap matters more than throughput and you accept unmaintained code.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing has been measured. The README says qajson4c got top scores in nativejson-benchmark's Parse Memory, Memory Peak and AllocCount categories, but that suite's only published results (2016-09-09, clang 7.0, Core i7-4980HQ, mac64/mac32) predate the qajson4c integration (PR #78, merged 2017-05-05) and have no qajson4c row. No figures exist against RapidJSON or nlohmann/json on any compiler or hardware.
status_note: Abandoned: last master commit 2019-03-22 (iterative_parsing branch 2019-11-01), and nativejson-benchmark still points at the old USESystemEngineeringBV location (PR #122 unmerged). It is MIT-licensed, about 2.1k lines of C99 and easy to vendor, but GCC/Clang only.
